subject: Binomial data is void (error causing inlaprogam to crash)

messages.author: 1ff9d6a9cb4114d9
messages.subject: Binomial data is void (error causing inlaprogam to crash)
parts:
Hello INLA experts, 

I am running a population abundance where the Y variable is abundance in a particular location - which is dispersed as such: 
Y: 
   0 = 2345
   1 = 295
   2 = 29
   3 = 1
   4 = 2
   
I have stacked the data as such : 
## Create data stack 
stk <- inla.stack(data=list(Y=Y,  Ntrials=n), A=list(A,1), tag="sdata",
                  effects=list(ind, list(data.frame(b0=1, covars))))

And built and run the model as such: 
## Model 0: no spatial or random effects 
form0 <- Y ~ 0 + b0 + ndvi + slp + sea + avgt + prec + seas + ag + op +of
res0  <- inla(form0, family = "binomial", data=inla.stack.data(stk),
              control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stk), compute=TRUE),
              control.fixed=fixed.priors, control.family=list(link="logit"),
              control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose = TRUE)

However I get this error: 

*** ERROR *** INLA.Data1: Binomial data[124] (nb,y) = (1,2) is void

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

The model runs fine when I re-code the Y variable to 0,1. I would like to know where I could possibly have gone wrong in setting up the data to allow for abundance data. 

Thank you!

parts:
yes, this is an error in the input, if y ~ binomial(n, p), then y=0...n,
and you have n=1 and y=2.

so here is how to recreate the error

> inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y=2), Ntrials=1, family="binomial")


*** ERROR *** INLA.Data1: Binomial data[0] (nb,y) = (1,2) is void
